"Through the darkness and mystery of their pain God draws
men unto Himself"
, writes Agnes Günther. We ought to
remember how uncertain are the brilliance and good fortune
of our lives, and in days of sunny prosperity we should be
prepared for God's call which summons us in the "dark night
of the soul" unto Himself.
And have we not to some extent already experienced how
this call of God, extremely inconvenient and disturbing as it
was, nevertheless became a blessing for us? Have we not
known how, just by being torn out of a life of custom and
routine, we have been preserved from inner torpidity and
indolence? That our life thus received a new impulse and a
new depth (whether through our own pain or through our
perception of another's sorrow) so that then for the first time
we realized what it meant to live? Have we not felt in such
circumstances that we enjoy more deeply and gratefully the
happiness that was given us to enjoy, and that we found a
new and closer link with our families? That in days of dark
distress we became more patient, and from hard times were
permitted to reap a harvest of blessing? How easy it is for us
to become buried in the sameness of the days; how easily we
are deadened by the routine of life, so that our personal life
and its spiritual condition grows to be a matter of indiffer-
ence to us! Or again, how easily we get agitated by things
which are not worth such excitement! God's call, extremely
disturbing and inconvenient as it is, shakes us up and causes
us to throw off our lethargy, restoring to us our true life and
enabling us once more to view things in their true per-
spective.
To be vigilantly prepared for the moment which is always
the decisive moment! The Christian faith of course is no
calm and static possession. It is not simply the conviction of
the truth of certain doctrines which can once for all be
assimilated. The Christian faith consists in a certain direc-
tion of the will. It is only alive in us if its reality is ever anew
proved and tested in the process of living. It is not sufficient
